concepts.title: Arithmetic Expressions and Values
concepts.definition: Mathematical phrases like 13 + 2, 20 – 4, 12 × 5, and 18 ÷ 3 are called arithmetic expressions. Every arithmetic expression has a value which is the number it evaluates to.
concepts.key_idea: An expression is a sequence of numbers and operations that results in a single numerical value.

concepts.title: Brackets in Expressions
concepts.definition: When evaluating anin short,  expression having brackets, we need to first find the values of the expressions inside the brackets before performing other operations.
concepts.key_idea: Brackets specify the order of operations to resolve ambiguity.

concepts.title: Terms in Expressions
concepts.definition: Terms are the parts of an expression separated by a ‘+’ sign. Subtractions are converted to additions of the inverse to identify terms.
concepts.key_idea: Expressions are sums of terms; multiplication and division results are treated as single terms.

concepts.title: Commutative Property of Addition
concepts.definition: Swapping the terms does not change the sum. This is called the commutative property of addition.
concepts.key_idea: The order of terms in an addition expression does not affect the final value.

concepts.title: Associative Property of Addition
concepts.definition: Grouping the terms of an expression in different ways gives the same value. This is called the associative property of addition.
concepts.key_idea: The way terms are grouped in addition does not change the result.

concepts.title: Removing Brackets Preceded by a Negative Sign
concepts.definition: Upon removing thesimply put,  brackets preceded by a negative sign, the signs of the terms inside the brackets change.
concepts.key_idea: A minus sign before a bracket acts on every term inside the bracket by flipping its sign.

concepts.title: Distributive Property
concepts.definition: The multiple of a sum (difference) is the same as the sum (difference) of the multiples. Also known as multiplying a number with an expression inside brackets.
concepts.formula: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c
concepts.key_idea: Multiplication distributes over addition and subtraction.
